# libdiginet / fuzz_codec

libdiginet's own fuzz target `fuzz_codec` ([source](source/fuzz_codec.c), unmodified), which OSS-Fuzz does not run, over libdiginet 0.1.1 (FreeMixer/libdiginet at 835f336c).

Reads the input as up to 256 operations, each calling one of the library's control encoders (fader, button, touch, V-Pot, jog, ring, meter, LEDs, scribble strip, counter, sysex) or text and display helpers with arguments taken from the input, for no desk, a Control|24 or a ProControl. Each result is compared with the bytes and ranges the protocol documentation and the library's header give, worked out by the harness itself. Inputs of 64 MiB or more are ignored.

## How this program differs from a libFuzzer build of this fuzz target
- Linked against libdiginet at commit 835f336c: the frame, command cursor, controls and decoder sources and the session state machine, built into one static library. The packet socket and descriptor io are not built; the library's own libFuzzer build uses the same sources.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the fuzz target one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
- Each desk personality is the one the protocol documentation describes and is found by its announce name; three other names ("CNTRL|2", "MAINUNITS" and the empty name) give no desk ([lines 256-281](source/fuzz_codec.c#L256-L281)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The sysex encoder never succeeds for the system-family function 0x70 ([lines 283-291](source/fuzz_codec.c#L283-L291)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each encoder succeeds exactly for the arguments its header comment allows, otherwise fails with the documented code and leaves the output command untouched ([lines 293-314](source/fuzz_codec.c#L293-L314)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- Each successful encoder writes the message the protocol documentation gives for the control, byte for byte, with a key naming its address, and marks only scribble and counter writes as display writes ([lines 316-344](source/fuzz_codec.c#L316-L344)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The scribble text helper writes the documented characters and reports how many input bytes it used ([lines 431-452](source/fuzz_codec.c#L431-L452)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The seven-segment helper lights, for each character, the segments a seven-segment display shows for it ([lines 454-466](source/fuzz_codec.c#L454-L466)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The counter text helper places digits and dots as the header documents ([lines 468-490](source/fuzz_codec.c#L468-L490)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.
- The meter mask and segment count and the ring dot and fill helpers light exactly what they name ([lines 492-519](source/fuzz_codec.c#L492-L519)): abort(); not confirmed in the binary.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libdiginet` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
